definition: JSGF stands for Java Speech Grammar Format or the JSpeech Grammar Format (in a W3C Note).
details: Developed by Sun Microsystems, it is a textual representation of grammars for use in speech recognition for technologies like XHTML+Voice. JSGF adopts the style and conventions of the Java programming language in addition to use of traditional grammar notations. The Speech Recognition Grammar Specification was derived from this specification.

explainer.lead: JSGF is a text format for telling a speech recognizer which words and phrases it should expect. It gives developers a compact way to describe valid speech, and it later informed the Speech Recognition Grammar Specification.

tiers.eli5: Imagine teaching a listening robot by handing it a menu of things people are allowed to say. JSGF is a way of writing that menu, such as offering only “coffee” or “tea.” The robot then knows to listen for those choices instead of every possible sentence.
tiers.practitioner: Use JSGF to write textual grammars for speech-recognition applications, including systems using XHTML+Voice. Its Java-style conventions and traditional grammar notation define the wording a recognizer should expect; do not confuse writing the grammar with implementing the recognizer itself.
tiers.paperLevel: JSGF (Java Speech Grammar Format, or JSpeech Grammar Format in a W3C Note) is a textual representation of recognition grammars, combining Java programming-language conventions with traditional grammar notation. Developed by Sun Microsystems, it specifies expected spoken forms rather than a recognition algorithm; the Speech Recognition Grammar Specification was derived from it.

explainer.example: A rule such as public <drink> = coffee | tea; defines a drink choice. Under that rule, the spoken word “tea” matches, while “hot chocolate” does not.

explainer.intuition: A JSGF grammar is like a phrasebook for a recognizer: it describes acceptable utterances in advance, narrowing what the system needs to listen for.
howItWorks: Write the grammar as text using JSGF conventions.
Define rules for the words or phrases speakers may say.
Provide the grammar to a speech-recognition application.
Use those rules to guide recognition of spoken input.
explainer.whyItMatters: JSGF provided a readable, text-based way to specify recognition grammars using familiar Java-style conventions. Its influence also extends through the Speech Recognition Grammar Specification, which was derived from it.
misconceptions: JSGF is a grammar notation, not a speech-recognition engine.
It borrows Java style and conventions but is not ordinary Java program code.
JSGF and the Speech Recognition Grammar Specification are not the same specification; the latter was derived from the former.
